title: Anger aimed at the bowl
literal_meaning: Biting the bowl in anger at the medicine.
explanation: The unpleasant thing is the medicine, but the anger is directed at its container. The expression describes displaced frustration: attacking a messenger, object or bystander instead of addressing the actual problem.
meaning_odia: ଔଷଧ ଉପରେ ରାଗ ହେଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ରାଗର ଆଘାତ ପଡ଼ିଲା ପାତ୍ର ଉପରେ। ଅସୁବିଧାର ମୂଳ ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଥାଇ ରାଗ ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଝାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ରାଗ କାହା ଉପରେ ହେଲା ଓ ତାହାର ଫଳ କିଏ ଭୋଗିଲା, ସେହି ଦୁଇଟିକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖିଲେ କଥାଟିର ମର୍ମ ବୁଝାପଡ଼େ।
usage_example: A delayed delivery frustrates a customer, who shouts at a neighbour merely passing on the update. Another person uses the saying to identify the misplaced anger. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The source writes ଓଷଦ and କାମୁଡିବା; this edition preserves those forms rather than silently replacing them with modern spellings. The image explains behaviour and gives no advice about taking medicine.

witnesses.note: Text and accompanying sense read in original community page; rewritten explanation, not historical-origin claim.

origin_note: First coinage, named author and regional distribution are not established. This entry records a contemporary digital witness; it does not prove exclusive Odia origin. No oral-history interview has been conducted.

odia_summary: ଯାହା ପାଇଁ ରାଗ, ତାହା ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟ ଉପରେ ରାଗ ସୁଝାଇବା।
english_summary: Anger falls on the container, messenger or bystander instead of the real cause of frustration.

graphic.alt: A seated adult gestures angrily toward a small bowl on a table.
graphic.caption: Frustration turns toward the wrong object.
